label: 0047 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 48 windows): 0046 with the 2009 Suruga Bay earthquake, shallow Mw 5.6–6.0 earthquakes and the 2000 Usu eruption (to 90 km) removed as steps and a tighter prior on the 2000–05 Tokai slow slip event, uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, eleven slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0046 after a follow-up to the residual search. The base experiment removes three sets of steps the earlier models left in. The 11 August 2009 Suruga Bay earthquake (JMA M6.5), missing from the Global CMT catalog, is removed as a step within 100 km. Shallow earthquakes (CMT depth 30 km or less) of Mw 5.6–6.0 are now steps too, among them Yamaguchi 1997, Iwate 1998, Awaji 2013 and Miyake-jima 2013. The 2000 Usu eruption is removed within 90 km instead of 30, since its step is still 2 mm at 70–90 km. Together they cut 2009–2011 residuals by 26% at Suruga and 23% at Tokai, 1997 residuals at Yamaguchi by 35%, and spring 2013 residuals in the Izu islands by 60%. Two places get worse: two Suruga sites in June–September 2011, and one Iwate site in 1998, where the 1998 intrusion beneath Iwate volcano is now exposed. The 2000–05 Tokai slow slip event gets a tighter prior (sd of total slip 50 mm instead of 150, taper 50 km instead of 80), which raises window cross-validation by 75. Its Mw drops from 7.17 to 6.99, within the range of published GEONET inversions (about 7.0–7.1); the data pin it only to about ±0.1, and Tokai background coupling in 2000–05 is 0.04–0.09 lower. Elsewhere the model matches 0046. Coupling far outside −1 to 1 isn't a real value: it is episode strike-slip, or Kumamoto afterslip, divided by a small plate rate. MAP solution, no posterior SD.
